facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a large herbivore that could walk on two or four legs and reached about 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: A large bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore around 8 m long

facts.statement: Gryposaurus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 80 to 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: lived about 80 to 75 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous (late Santonian to late Campanian stages) of North America

facts.statement: A possible species from the Javelina Formation in Texas might extend the genus's temporal range to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: A possible additional species from the Javelina Formation in Texas may extend the temporal range of the genus to 66 million years ago

facts.statement: Gryposaurus may have preferred riverine habitats.
facts.quote: it may have preferred river settings

facts.statement: William Parks named a skeleton from the Dinosaur Park Formation as Kritosaurus incurvimanus rather than Gryposaurus incurvimanus, reflecting the debate over whether the two genera were synonymous.
facts.quote: This idea was reflected in William Parks's naming of a nearly complete skeleton from the Dinosaur Park Formation as Kritosaurus incurvimanus, not Gryposaurus incurvimanus

facts.statement: Current research suggests that Hadrosaurus can be distinguished from Gryposaurus based on differences in the upper arm and ilium.
facts.quote: Current thought is that Hadrosaurus, although known from fragmentary material, can be distinguished from Gryposaurus by differences in the upper arm and ilium

facts.statement: Further research revealed a second species, G. latidens, found in slightly older rocks in Montana compared to the classic Alberta localities.
facts.quote: Further research has revealed the presence of a second species, G. latidens, from slightly older rocks in Montana than the classic gryposaur localities of Alberta

facts.statement: New material from the Kaiparowits Formation in Utah represents the species G. monumentensis.
facts.quote: New material from the Kaiparowits Formation of Utah, in Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument, includes a skull and partial skeleton that represent the species G. monumentensis

facts.statement: The type species of Gryposaurus is G. notabilis.
facts.quote: type_species: Gryposaurus notabilis

facts.statement: Recognized species of Gryposaurus include G. notabilis (Lambe, 1914), G. latidens (Horner, 1992), G. monumentensis (Gates & Sampson, 2007), and the questionable G. alsatei (Lehman, Wick, Wagner, 2016).
facts.quote: subdivision: G. notabilisLambe, 1914 G. latidensHorner, 1992 G. monumentensisGates & Sampson, 2007 G. alsatei?Lehman, Wick, Wagner, 2016

facts.statement: As of 2016, three species are recognized as valid: G. notabilis, G. latidens, and G. monumentensis.
facts.quote: As of 2016, there are currently three named species that are recognized as valid today: G. notabilis, G. latidens, and G. monumentensis

facts.statement: The informal name "Hadrosauravus" was an early, unused name for G. latidens.
facts.quote: The informal name "Hadrosauravus" is an early, unused name for this species

facts.statement: G. latidens has a nasal arch farther forward on the snout than G. notabilis and teeth that reflect iguanodont-like characteristics.
facts.quote: Its nasal arch is prominent like that of G. notabilis, but farther forward on the snout, and its teeth are less derived, reflecting iguanodont-like characteristics

facts.statement: The type specimen of Gryposaurus notabilis represents an animal approximately 8.2 meters long.
facts.quote: one of the best specimens of this genus, the nearly complete type specimen of Kritosaurus incurvimanus (now regarded as a synonym of Gryposaurus notabilis) came from an animal about 8.2 m long.

facts.statement: Skin impressions show that Gryposaurus had scutes up to 3.8 centimeters long on its flanks and tail.
facts.quote: showing this dinosaur to have had several different types of scalation: pyramidal, ridged, limpet-shaped feature scales forming scutes upwards of 3.8 centimeters long (1.5 inches) on the flank and tail

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Gryposaurus latidens to be 7.5 meters long and 2.5 metric tons in mass.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated the size of G. latidens at 7.5 m in length and 2.5 MT in body mass

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Gryposaurus notabilis and G. monumentensis to be 8 meters long and 3 metric tons in mass.
facts.quote: the other two species (G. notabilis and G. monumentensis) at 8 m in length and 3 MT in body mass

facts.statement: The prominent nasal arch of Gryposaurus is formed by paired nasal bones.
facts.quote: The prominent nasal arch found in this genus is formed from the paired nasal bones.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a saurolophine hadrosaurid, a type of duckbill dinosaur without hollow head crests.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus was a saurolophine (hadrosaurine of older references) hadrosaurid, a member of the duckbill subfamily without hollow head crests.

facts.statement: Jack Horner coined the subfamily Gryposaurinae, but this classification is no longer in use.
facts.quote: A subfamily, Gryposaurinae, was coined by Jack Horner as part of a larger revision that promoted Hadrosaurinae to family status, but is not now in use.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus has been proposed as a synonym of Gryposaurus, though it is slightly younger.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus has been proposed to be a synonym of Gryposaurus, but it is slightly younger.

facts.statement: The genus Gryposaurus was named by Lambe in 1914.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Lambe, 1914

facts.statement: The type species of Gryposaurus is Gryposaurus notabilis.
facts.quote: type_species: Gryposaurus notabilis

facts.statement: Known species include Gryposaurus latidens (Horner, 1992), Gryposaurus monumentensis (Gates & Sampson, 2007), and the dubious Gryposaurus alsatei (Lehman et al., 2016).
facts.quote: subdivision: Gryposaurus latidens Horner, 1992 Gryposaurus monumentensis Gates & Sampson, 2007 Gryposaurus alsatei? Lehman, Wick, Wagner, 2016

facts.statement: Gryposaurus lived between 85 and 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del periodo Cretácico hace aproximadamente entre 85 y 66 millones de años, entre el Santoniense y el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The type species Gryposaurus notabilis is from the Late Campanian Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es Gryposaurus notabilis de la Formación Dinosaur Park de Alberta, Canadá, del Campaniense tardío

facts.statement: Gryposaurus latidens is from the Santonian Dos Medicinas Formation of Montana, USA.
facts.quote: la segunda especie nombrada fue Gryposaurus latidens de la Formación Dos Medicina del Santoniense de Montana, EE. UU.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus monumentensis is from the Campanian Kaiparowits Formation of Utah, USA.
facts.quote: la tercera especie considerada válida es Gryposaurus monumentensis de la Formación Kaiparowits en Utah, EE. UU. también del Campaniense.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus alsatei is from the Late Maastrichtian Javelina Formation of Texas, USA, and is considered dubious.
facts.quote: Por último la especie Gryposaurus alsatei de la Formación Javelina en Texas EE. UU., que data del Maastrichtiense tardío, siendo considerada dudosa.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore that ate a variety of plants.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Gryposaurus would have been a bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore, eating a variety of plants.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus had skull joints allowing a grinding motion and dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at once.
facts.quote: Its skull had special joints that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing, and its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Gryposaurus was both a grazer and a browser, feeding on tough, fibrous plant material.
facts.quote: The paleontologists who unearthed G. monumentensis back in the 2000s brought the fact that this creature dined on tough, fibrous plant material which would imply that Gryposaurs was both a grazer and a browser.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the smooth dental microwear of a single specimen reflects the overall feeding patterns of Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: However, because only one specimen had dental microwear texture analysis performed on it, this may not reflect the overall feeding patterns of this taxon.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus may have preferred habitats related to rivers.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus may have preferred river-related settings.

facts.statement: The nasal arch of Gryposaurus may have been used for social functions like identifying sexes or species and establishing social ranking.
facts.quote: The distinctive nasal arch of Gryposaurus, like other cranial modifications in duckbills, may have been used for a variety of social functions, such as identification of sexes or species and social ranking.

facts.statement: The nasal arch may have been used for pushing or butting in contests, possibly aided by inflatable air sacs for signaling.
facts.quote: It could also have functioned as a tool for broadside pushing or butting in social contests, and there may have been inflatable air sacs flanking it for both visual and auditory signaling.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the Kaiparowits Formation site was near the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: During the Late Cretaceous period, the site of the Kaiparowits Formation was located near the western shore of the Western Interior Seaway, a large inland sea that split North America into two landmasses, Laramidia to the west and Appalachia to the east.

facts.statement: The habitat was an ancient floodplain with large channels, wetland swamps, ponds, and lakes, bordered by highlands.
facts.quote: The plateau where dinosaurs lived was an ancient floodplain dominated by large channels and abundant wetland peat swamps, ponds and lakes, and was bordered by highlands.

facts.statement: The climate was wet and humid, supporting an abundant and diverse range of organisms.
facts.quote: The climate was wet and humid, and supported an abundant and diverse range of organisms.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus monumentensis shared its environment with dromaeosaurids, troodontids, ornithomimids, tyrannosaurids, ankylosaurids, Parasaurolophus, various ceratopsians, and Hagryphus.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus monumentensis shared its paleoenvironment with other dinosaurs, such as dromaeosaurid theropods, the troodontid Talos sampsoni, ornithomimids like Ornithomimus velox, tyrannosaurids like Albertosaurus and Teratophoneus, armored ankylosaurids, the duckbilled hadrosaur Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus, the ceratopsians Utahceratops gettyi, Nasutoceratops titusi and Kosmoceratops richardsoni and the oviraptorosaurian Hagryphus giganteus.

facts.statement: The Kaiparowits Formation also contained sharks, rays, amphibians, reptiles, and early mammals like multituberculates and marsupials.
facts.quote: Other paleofauna present in the Kaiparowits Formation included chondrichthyans (sharks and rays), frogs, salamanders, turtles, lizards and crocodilians. A variety of early mammals were present including multituberculates, marsupials, and insectivorans.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is distinguished by a narrow arched nasal hook, sometimes described as a "Roman nose," used for species or sexual identification and combat.
facts.quote: Se distingue más fácilmente de otros dinosaurios de pico de pato por su gancho nasal de arco estrecho, que a veces se describe como similar a la " nariz romana " y que puede haber sido utilizada para la identificación de especies o sexual y combate con individuos de la misma especie. especies.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a large herbivore about 9 meters long that could walk on two or four legs and preferred living near rivers.
facts.quote: Fue un gran herbívoro que podía avanzar de forma bípeda como cuadrúpeda de alrededor de 9 metros de largo, que preferiría vivir junto a los ríos.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus was a typical-sized hadrosaurid measuring approximately 9 meters long and 4 meters high.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus era un hadrosaúrido de tamaño y forma típicos, medía aproximadamente 9 metros de largo y 4 de alto.

facts.statement: The most robust of the four known species, G. monumentensis, may have reached 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: De las cuatro especies conocidas la más robusta es G. monumentensis que puede haber llegado a los 10 metros.

facts.statement: A nearly complete specimen shows skin impressions indicating various scales, including pyramidal, grooved, and large shell-like shields over 3.8 centimeters long on the flank and tail.
facts.quote: Este espécimen también tiene el mejor ejemplo de impresiones de piel para Gryposaurus , mostrando que este dinosaurio ha tenido varios tipos diferentes de escamación, piramidal, acanalada, escudos como lapa de más de 3,8 centímetros de largo en el flanco y la cola.

facts.statement: The prominent nasal arch of this genus is formed by paired nasal bones.
facts.quote: El arco nasal prominente que se encuentra en este género se forma a partir de los huesos nasales pareados .

facts.statement: In profile, the nasal arch rises into a rounded hump in front of the eyes, reaching a height as high as the top of the back of the skull.
facts.quote: En vista de perfil, se elevan en una joroba redondeada delante de los ojos, alcanzando una altura tan alta como el punto más alto de la parte posterior del cráneo.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus exhibited one of the highest numbers of teeth among dinosaurs, with about 300 active and nearly 800 total including replacement teeth.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus exhiben uno de los mayores números de dientes entre los dinosaurios, presentando unos 300 activos y en total cerca de 800 si se cuentan los de reemplazo.

facts.statement: This dental feature, combined with jaw articulation, allowed them to chew a wide variety of plants.
facts.quote: Esta característica, sumada a la articulación de la mandíbulas, les permitía masticar una amplia variedad de plantas.

facts.statement: It is believed the nasal arch held a skin sac that could be inflated to make a sound for social communication, and it is speculated that males raised skin coloration during mating season to increase blood flow.
facts.quote: del que se cree que sostuvo una bolsa de piel la cual podía llenar de aire para hacerla sonar, tuvo una función social de comunicación dentro de la manada y también se especula que los machos en época de apareamiento se exhibían subiendo el tono del color, aumentando así su irrigación.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is based on specimen NMC 2278, found in 1913 by George F. Sternberg in the Dinosaur Park Formation along the Red Deer River.
facts.quote: Gryposaurus está basado en el ejemplar NMC 2278, encontrado en 1913 por George F. Sternberg en la Formación Dinosaur Park en el Río Red Deer.

facts.statement: This specimen was described by Lawrence Lambe, who was particularly interested in the nasal arch.
facts.quote: Este espécimen fue descrito por Lawrence Lambe, donde le llamó la atención el arco nasal.

facts.statement: A 1942 influential monograph by Lull and Wright settled the synonymy between Kritosaurus and Gryposaurus for nearly fifty years in favor of Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: La publicación de 1942 de la influyente monografía de Lull y Wright sobre los hadrosáuridos selló la cuestión de la sinonimia entre Kritosaurus y Gryposaurus por casi cincuenta años a favor de Kritosaurus.

facts.statement: However, revisions beginning in the 1990s questioned the identity of Kritosaurus navajovius, which has limited material for comparison with other duck-billed dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, las revisiones que comenzaron en la década de 1990 pusieron en tela de juicio la identidad de Kritosaurus navajovius, que tiene material limitado para comparación con otros picos de pato.

facts.statement: Therefore, Gryposaurus has been separated from Kritosaurus again, at least temporarily.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Gryposaurus se ha vuelto a separar, al menos temporalmente, de Kritosaurus.

facts.statement: Gryposaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, approximately 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gryposaurus belongs to the parent group Kritosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Kritosaurini

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Gryposaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
